text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY

- President Boris Yeltsin joined Patriarch Alexiy, head of the Russian Orthodox Church, at the consecration ceremony of a Moscow chapel in a bid to heal a rift between him and the clergy over a controversial religious law.

- First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais has instructed the Central Bank to take over operating control of the Customs Committee accounts, a move potentially damaging to Uneximbank, the paper said.

- The Association of Russian Banks and the Central Bank chairman Sergei Dubinin have expressed concern over moves by investigators into alleged illegal deals involving certain commercial banks, saying they could damage the banking system as a whole.
- The Russian equities market has reacted calmly to plans for an investigation into the Norilsk Nickel smelter auction because it does not believe the results of the sell-off can be reversed.

- The board of directors of Noyabrskneftegaz oil company has voted for an additional share issue to pay back the company's debts to the budget in cash in an apparent attempt to avert any possibility of the oil giant being handed over to a new owner.
- Tax police in St Petersburg have frozen the correspondent accounts of 14 major Baltic banks, saying they colluded with Russian clients trying to dodge tax payments.

- President Yeltsin has met the head of the Russian gas monopoly Gazprom to discuss the company's stance on gas deliveries to Ukraine in the run-up to top-level negotiations with Turkmenistan President Saparmurat Niyazov, whose country also has interests in the Ukrainian gas market.
- Moscow is ready to mediate in the conflict between North and South Korea.
- Russian gold-miners set tough conditions to the government to prop up the ailing industry instead of letting commercial banks beef up their balances in speculative gold deals.
- Visa International credit card operator after a two-year search has not been able to find a viable Russian bank to run its operations in Russia and has chosen Citibank as its partner.

- International financier George Soros' remarks that he was ready to invest heavily in the Russian Rosneft oil producer have sent the company's shares rocketing, while Soros seemingly has lost interest in the bid and has quietly withdrawn his non-binding proposal.
- Russian Sibneft oil company and Salomon Brothers investment bank have worked out a scheme allowing them to legally avoid Russian internal taxation of the company's Eurobond issue.
SEVODNYA
- Sberbank, contrary to popular belief that it is the biggest handler of state money, lags far behind the Uneximbank for the amount of budget funds landing on its accounts.
- Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin managed to raise the auction price for the state stake in Norilsk Nickel by $80 million during a meeting with the main bidder, Uneximbank's head Vladimir Potanin.
- The Caspian sea oil reserves spark a growing row between its adjacent states, each seeking a bigger piece of the pie.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- Moscow and Grozny seem to be working behind the scenes on a comprehensive document which will determine their future relations.
- Russian small and medium business representatives urge the president to put an end to interminable harassments by tax authorities.
- Russian automakers have seen their share of the Central Asian market shrink in the onslaught of South Korean producers.
- Russia is evicting Turkmenistan from the CIS gas market.
IZVESTIA

- High-profile scandals which followed a string of auctions at which the state was selling off its stake in some of Russia's most profitable enterprises have proved the government is unable to avoid the legal traps it had set itself.

- Local companies in the Krasnodar region in southern Russia are looking into the possibility of skimming some profits from the pipeline to be built in the region to transport oil from the Caspian Sea towards Europe.
- The Russian foreign ministry, hard-hit by an unprecedented brain-drain at the beginning of the decade, seems to be getting over its personnel crisis.
- Aman Tuleyev, newly-appointed governor of the coal-mining Kuzbass region, is working overtime to become the one and only leader of the troubled region.
- Russian arms dealers see South-East Asia as a market where they could push aside powerful competitors from the U.S. and Europe.
ROSSIISKAYA GAZETA
- Russians have been slow to react to the news about a redenomination of the rouble due to start next year.
- Sberbank and Vnesheconombank are the only commercial banks in Russia to which the government can entrust the budget money and keep its peace of mind.

- President Boris Yeltsin has thrown his weight behind the young reformer in the government, First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov, recently the target of attacks in the mass media controlled by powerful financial groups. MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS

- A thief who was stealing war-time decorations from World War II veterans in Moscow was looking up the names of his future victims in the official Soviet-era encyclopaedia. --Andrei Shukshin, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
